title: Royalist letters in Abraham Cowley's hand ('Mr. Conleys Hand'), Paris 28 Dec 1652 and 3 May 1653 (BL Harley MS 7003 ff. 314-315; DECODE R7768, R7769)

documents.shelfmark: BL Harley MS 7003 ff. 314r-314v; DECODE R7768

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the fair copy.

transcription.notes: Four runs of colon-separated numbers inside clear English; the whole letter is in transcription.txt.

documents.shelfmark: BL Harley MS 7003 ff. 314v-315r; DECODE R7769

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the fair copy.

transcription.source: Authenticated DECODE images IMG_R7769_I35117_P1-P2 (P1 is byte-identical to R7768 P2)
transcription.notes: One code group (Mr 203) in the postscript.

system.summary: Colon-separated numbers up to 248 inside clear English: a few code words and names apparently spelled letter by letter.

prior_solution.where: Not in Miscellanea Aulica (1702), Cowley's printed letters to Bennet; no other print found. Clarendon State Papers calendar not checked.

conditions.human_role: Selected the target from the catalogue; the DECODE session cookie was supplied earlier.

solution.what: Downloaded the four DECODE images of R7768/R7769; f.314v is imaged on both records.
Transcribed both letters; the docket reads 'mr Cowleys Hand' (DECODE: 'Conleys'); 23 code numbers in five runs.
Searched Miscellanea Aulica (1702) full text for Cowley's letters and web for distinctive clear phrases: not printed there.
Applied the Hyde-Barwick key (1659) to the five runs: gibberish.
Place run 248:88:46:47:96:52:7:57 = 'Scotland' from context (assistance next spring, Glencairn rising); unverified, grade M.

outcome.method_basis: The clear text of both letters was read but the 23 code numbers were not: no key on DECODE or in print, and the Hyde-Barwick key does not fit.
outcome.notes: Clear text read; the 23 code numbers are too few for a ciphertext-only attack and no Jermyn/Queen key of 1652-53 was found.
